narrative:
On October 1, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 46.4%, hearing 1,314 out of 2,832 scheduled matters across 55 judges. This represents an efficiency rebound from the previous day's hearing rate of 39.5% (1,169 of 2,960 heard on September 30), bringing throughput closer to levels recorded on September 28 (45.5%) and September 29 (49.1%).

Stage-level conversion showed significant recovery in disposals. The court’s heaviest procedural stage, Orders, converted at 48.3% (484 of 1,002 matters heard), up from 43.8% on September 30. Admissions followed with a 49.4% hearing rate (374 of 757 heard). Final Hearings exhibited the sharpest turnaround, converting 35.8% (156 of 436 heard) compared to just 19.7% the day before. Among case types, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the bulk of the docket and saw their hearing rate jump from 36.3% on September 30 to 50.4% (535 of 1,061 heard). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) and Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) also registered balanced clearance at 49.2% and 49.1% respectively, whereas Regular First Appeals (RFA) lagged considerably at 14.6%.

Benches demonstrated stark contrasts in operational clearance. Maintaining high throughput noted across previous days, Justice T.P. Vivekananda heard 84.6% of a 52-matter list in Hall 36. Similarly, Justice V. Srishananda (Hall 23) and Justice K.S. Hemalekha (Hall 30) cleared substantial volume, hearing 73 of 99 (73.7%) and 74 of 99 (74.7%) matters respectively. In contrast, several benches recorded zero hearings despite heavy cause lists, most notably Hall 24 under Justice Hanchate Sanjeevkumar (0 of 95 heard) and the Division Bench in Hall 3 comprising Justices Jayant Banerji and N.V. Bhavani (0 of 67 heard).
